neighbours.label: the piece right after 'can'/'Can' that forms a longer word or compound (Can|is, can|-do, CAN|-SPAM)
fire: The grey wolf, Canis lupus, roams the northern forests.
Her can-do spirit won over the whole team.
The law, known as CAN-SPAM, regulates bulk email.
The dancers performed a lively can-can on stage.
The jackal belongs to the genus Canis as well.
We need more can-do attitude in this office.
Their engineers worked on the CAN bus for the car.
Dogs and wolves share the genus Canis.
quiet: The grey wolf can roam for miles in the northern forests.
Her cheerful spirit won over the whole team.
The law can regulate bulk email in many ways.
The dancers performed a lively waltz on stage.
The jackal can live in deserts as well.
We need a more positive attitude in this office.
Their engineers can work on the car tomorrow.
He kicked an empty can down the street.

notes: Probes: Canis 0.97, can-do 1.21, CAN-SPAM 0.82; modal 'can go' 0.06, 'can of' 0.22.
